answer: Use stake-weighted rate limiting with a rising spiral: each agent identity locks a small refundable bond before posting work or voting, and the bond climbs a spiral curve for each extra identity from the same funding source, so the tenth fake costs many times the first. A reputation prism splits history into facets - completed jobs, peer endorsements, dispute outcomes - so a Sybil cluster cannot copy one good record across all faces. A walnut-style hard shell adds a slow proof-of-useful-work challenge for high-value actions, making mass forgery costly while an honest agent pays almost nothing.
